title: High Contrast (forced colours), text size, Calm and colour-only indicators
owns: app/renderer/shared/ember.css and the forced-colors / text-size / Calm rules in every renderer's styles.css; the handle's and ask box's indicator markup only as far as the findings need

findings.title: No forced-colors support: under Windows contrast themes switches, the slider, selection state, focus rings and button edges disappear
findings.area: All windows: Windows High Contrast / contrast themes (WCAG 1.4.1, 1.4.11, 2.4.7, 4.1.2)
findings.scenario: A Windows 10/11 user with a contrast theme (Settings > Accessibility > Contrast themes) opens Ember. In settings: the 'Listen for Hey Ember', 'Speak replies', 'Start Ember when I log in' and Calm mode switches are invisible (no track, no knob, no on/off), the Size slider is invisible, the selected character card is not marked, the status dots are gone, and the 'Remove' buttons are plain text. Keyboard focus is invisible everywhere. The command window shows 'Allow' and 'Not now' as bare words with no button shape or primary distinction, and the selected tab is not marked (every tab looks the same). The overlay's task cards lose their state symbol (ring, question mark, tick, cross), so 'working vs failed' is not shown at all. The bubble's Allow and Not now lose their capsules and focus ring. Everything stays unchanged for the screen reader.
findings.evidence: No @media (forced-colors) rule or forced-color-adjust anywhere (grep over app/ and packages/ CSS and bubble.ts). Chromium run with forcedColors:'active' (forced.mjs, forced2.mjs, forced3.mjs). Screenshots: scratchpad/release-review/ux-a11y/home-forced.png, home-forced-voice.png, forced-active-switch-focus.png (compare forced-none-switch-focus.png), forced-active-btn-focus.png (no ring on the focused 'Remove KeePassXC'), overlay-forced.png (cards have no symbol), cmd-forced.png. Cause: all control chrome is drawn with background-color, box-shadow and mask-background, which forced colors remove or override. Examples: ember.css:195 `.btn:focus-visible { outline:none; box-shadow:… }`, the switch rules at ember.css:207-232, overlay/styles.css:57-58 (.task::before mask), bubble.ts:292-306 (.eb-actions button), home/styles.css:85-101 (range) and 100-ish (.card). The overlay stays transparent in forced colors (alpha 0 verified), so it is not a screen-covering bug. PLAN.md manual item 14 ('Windows contrast themes keep the bubble readable') is still owed.
findings.fix: Add an @media (forced-colors: active) block to ember.css, bubble.ts BUBBLE_CSS and each page's styles. Give every control a real 1px ButtonText border. Replace outline:none with outline:2px solid Highlight on :focus-visible. Draw the switch with a border and a Highlight-filled checked state. Set forced-color-adjust:none on mask symbols and dots and fill them with CanvasText, LinkText or GrayText. Give the selected card and tab an outline or border, and the slider a ButtonText track and thumb. Then run PLAN item 14 on a real Windows contrast theme.

findings.title: Windows High Contrast (forced colours) is unsupported: switches, slider, selected character and focus rings disappear
findings.scenario: A Windows 10/11 user on a Contrast theme opens Settings. Every switch (Listen for “Hey Ember”, Start at login, Calm mode, every Run commands switch) is invisible, so neither its position nor its state can be seen. The size slider has no track or thumb. The chosen character card has no ring or tick. Buttons lose their borders. The keyboard focus ring (a box-shadow with outline:none) is gone everywhere, so a keyboard user cannot see where focus is.
findings.evidence: No `forced-colors` rule exists in app/renderer (grep). Chromium rendered with forcedColors:'active': /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Ember-Powered-by-Github-Copilot/9df81ff3-d6fa-5078-ac02-9c8dbaa6cb03/scratchpad/release-review/ux-home/forced-top.png and forced-top2.png. Dark and Increase Contrast shots for comparison: lm-dark-same.png and lm-contrast.png. Adding the CSS in forced-fix.css (same folder) restores them: forced-top2-with-fix.png.
findings.fix: Add an `@media (forced-colors: active)` block. Give switches `border:1px solid ButtonText; background:Canvas` with a ButtonText knob, and `:checked` using Highlight/HighlightText. Give .btn, .card, .group and inputs 1px ButtonText borders. Mark the selected card with `outline:3px solid Highlight`. Draw the slider track and thumb with system colours and `forced-color-adjust:none`. Replace box-shadow focus rings with a real `outline: 2px solid Highlight`. forced-fix.css is a working starting point.

findings.title: Windows Contrast themes (forced-colors) make switches, the consent checkbox, slider, character selection, button edges and all state symbols invisible
findings.area: Accessibility settings: forced-colors / high contrast (all windows)
findings.platforms: windows (Contrast themes in Win10/11; Chromium forced-colors on any OS)
findings.scenario: A low-vision user on Windows with a Contrast theme (Aquatic, Desert, High Contrast Black or White) installs Ember. The first-run screen shows 'I've read how Ember works and I agree' with no visible checkbox and a bare 'Start Ember' word with no button shape, so the consent gate cannot be seen. After setup, every switch in Settings, the Size slider, the selected-character ring and tick, 'Sign out', 'Add', the select boxes and the text fields have no outline or fill. In the command window 'Allow' and 'Not now' are floating words, the selected tab is indistinguishable, and the done, failed and stopped symbols are gone. The overlay task cards lose their working, failed and needs-you symbols, and the handle loses its mic dot, so state is no longer conveyed at all. Everything is built from background-colour, mask and box-shadow, and forced-colors drops all three. No CSS or JS in the app mentions forced-colors, and docs/DESIGN.md says Increase Contrast reaches every surface; on Windows that mechanism is forced-colors, not prefers-contrast.
findings.evidence: Emulated forced-colors:active with prefers-contrast:more (dark and light) in Chromium 141 and rendered every page. Computed styles in that mode: #login and #login::before background rgb(255,255,255) (Canvas), box-shadow none, border 0; .btn.quiet, select, text input, .card[aria-checked=true] and .group box-shadow none; .card::after (the tick mask) and .dot background Canvas. grep for 'forced-colors|forcedColors|HighContrast' across app/, docs/ and test/ finds nothing relevant. Screenshots: shots/home-forced-dark.png, shots/home-first-forced-light.png (the checkbox and Start button are missing), shots/overlay-forced-light.png, shots/overlay-forced-dark.png, shots/content-forced-combo.png (command window and prompt cards). Harness: forced-home.mjs, forced-first.mjs, shot-forced-float.mjs, shot-content.mjs, forced-css.mjs.
findings.fix: Add one @media (forced-colors: active) block to ember.css (it reaches every page) and mirror it in the bubble CSS. Give controls real borders in system colours: .btn, .start, .card, select, input, .tab, .eb-actions button, .task-actions button and the overlay and handle buttons get border:1px solid ButtonText. For the switch use border:2px solid ButtonText, ::before background ButtonText, and :checked background Highlight with ::before HighlightText. For the checkbox use a 1px ButtonText border and a CanvasText tick when checked. For the slider use a ButtonText track and thumb. For .card[aria-checked=true] use outline:3px solid Highlight. For every mask symbol (.task::before, .tab::before, .pending-line::before, .card::after, .dot, .mic, .eb-dot, the sidebar tiles and the terms icons) set forced-color-adjust:none and background:CanvasText (or Highlight). Keep the glass as Canvas with a ButtonText border. Re-run the forced-colors emulation to confirm.

findings.title: Windows High Contrast (forced-colors): state symbols, the status dot and the Stop/Close button edges disappear
findings.scenario: With a Windows contrast theme on, Chromium forces colours: the task cards' state symbols are a mask filled with background-color (forced to Canvas), the status pill's dot is a background, and Stop/Close are drawn only with a box-shadow edge and no border, which forced-colors removes. Each card then has no running/failed/done symbol and Stop/Close look like bare text, although the design rule is 'never colour alone, symbol beside the words on every surface'. The nothing in app/ or packages/ handles forced-colors (only prefers-contrast).
findings.evidence: Playwright with forcedColors:'active' (s3.mjs): s3-forced.png and s3-forced-light.png show cards with no symbols, a pill with no dot, 'Stop'/'Close' with no edge, and the bubble chip dot missing. grep for forced-colors / forced-color-adjust across app and packages returns nothing.
findings.fix: Add @media (forced-colors: active) rules: .task::before and .status i get background: CanvasText/Highlight (forced-color-adjust: none) or use a border-based symbol; .task-actions button gets border: 1px solid ButtonText; keep the ring's border (it already survives). Do the same for the bubble chip dot and handle.

findings.title: Windows High Contrast: Allow, Not now, Stop and tabs lose their borders, and keyboard focus is invisible
findings.area: design system: forced colours on confirm and command UI
findings.scenario: A low-vision user runs Windows with a contrast theme. On the ask card, Allow, Not now and Stop render as bare words: .btn is 'all: unset' and draws its edge and focus ring with box-shadow, which forced-colors mode removes. The command block, card and tab borders vanish and the selected tab can't be told from the others. With Tab on Allow, nothing shows where focus is.
findings.evidence: forced.mjs with Playwright forcedColors:'active' (shots/Q-forced-colors.png): buttons are plain text, no ring while document.activeElement is Allow. grep -rn 'forced-colors' app packages finds nothing; ember.css:195 uses outline:none; box-shadow for focus. DESIGN.md covers prefers-contrast but not forced-colors.
findings.fix: Add @media (forced-colors: active) to ember.css: give .btn, .tab and .command a real 1px border (border: 1px solid ButtonText, selected tab Highlight), and focus-visible { outline: 2px solid Highlight; outline-offset: 2px } on controls, tabs and .command.

findings.title: Increase Contrast: the keyboard focus ring is the same colour as accent-filled controls, so focus on primary buttons, checked switches and the selected character card is not visible as a ring
findings.area: Accessibility settings: Increase Contrast and focus visibility
findings.platforms: all (macOS Increase Contrast, GNOME high contrast, Windows when forced-colors is off)
findings.scenario: With the OS asking for more contrast, --focus-ring becomes '0 0 0 3px var(--accent)' and --accent is #ffa056. Every prominent control is also filled with var(--accent): .btn, .start, the command card's Allow, the prompt's 'Install and connect', the bubble and handle primary buttons, checked switches and checkboxes, and the selected card's inner ring. Tabbing onto one only makes it look 3 px bigger. There is no separate ring, so a keyboard user cannot tell which of 'Not now' and 'Install and connect' (or 'Allow') is focused before pressing Enter. In normal mode the ring is 75% orange, a faint dark band at about 1.6:1 against the button.
findings.evidence: Pixel scan across the left edge of a keyboard-focused primary button at 2x (prompt consent card): default mode ring (195,113,40) then button (255,146,48); Increase Contrast mode (255,160,86) all the way from the ring into the button, with no edge. Screenshot: shots/focus-primary-combo.png (top: default, bottom: Increase Contrast). The home Tab walk (walk-home.mjs) shows large pixel diffs on every stop, but only because the ring grows the shape.
findings.fix: Make the ring two-tone so it separates from accent fills, for example --focus-ring: 0 0 0 2px var(--surface-0), 0 0 0 5px var(--label) in prefers-contrast:more (and a surface-coloured 2 px gap under the accent ring in normal mode for filled controls). Apply it to the bubble's and handle's own focus rules, which reuse the token.

findings.title: Handle's microphone badge is colour-only (orange / grey / red 8 px dot) and sits on Cinder's orange mitten
findings.scenario: The only on-screen sign that Ember's microphone is open, muted or broken is an 8 px dot at the lower right of the face: accent orange while listening or waiting, grey when muted, red on error. With the default Cinder character that orange dot lands on Cinder's right mitten and reads as a second hand. With the other three characters it is a plain orange dot with no mic shape. For a colour-blind user, orange and red are close and there is no symbol or word. The tooltip only helps on hover, and the handle window is focusable:false, so assistive tech never reads it. This breaks the design's own 'never colour alone' rule for the one privacy-relevant indicator.
findings.evidence: Rendered the handle at 3x for all four characters, waiting vs muted: shots/mic-chars.png (the Cinder row shows a mitten and a dot side by side). Code: handle/main.ts sets mic.title only; .mic is an <i aria-hidden> with background colours (handle/styles.css:99-105).
findings.fix: Draw a small mic glyph (a slashed mic when muted, an exclamation when it has a problem) in a dark glass disc, or put the indicator beside the text line instead of on the face. Keep the accent for 'listening'. Add the state word to the line while the mic is in an error state, and expose it in the live region for the no-compositor card.

findings.title: Handle's microphone and computer-state dots are colour-only and hidden from assistive technology
findings.scenario: The persistent 'is my microphone listening, muted or broken' indicator is an 8 px dot (orange, grey or red) whose words live only in a title tooltip on an aria-hidden <i>. Colour-blind users cannot tell orange from red, and screen-reader users get nothing. The remote computer's state dot (green, amber, grey, red) is also colour-only visually (the words are only in the tooltip and aria-label). 'Microphone off' is shown as text for 2.5 s after toggling (main.ts:845) and then is gone.
findings.evidence: handle/index.html `<i id='mic' class='mic' hidden aria-hidden='true'>`; handle/styles.css:25-28 and 52-58; handle/main.ts:119 sets only title.
findings.fix: Add a short visible or sr-only word to the handle line ('Mic off', 'Hearing you') or a distinct shape per state, and expose it in the handle's accessible text.

findings.title: Mic badge: 8 px colour-only dot, hidden from assistive tech, error state unexplained
findings.scenario: The only sign that "Hey Ember" is listening, muted or broken is an 8 px dot on the face: orange (waiting), orange with halo (hearing you), grey (muted), red (error). A colour-blind user cannot tell orange from red reliably, and a screen-reader user gets nothing (the dot is aria-hidden). On a denied microphone permission or a lost device the pill reads "Ready" beside a red dot; the only words are a hover tooltip, "Microphone problem", with no way forward (the menu does not mention it). The states needs-models, downloading and starting show no dot, so "Hey Ember" silently does nothing.
findings.evidence: handle/index.html:14 `<i id="mic" class="mic" hidden aria-hidden="true">`; styles.css:99 `.mic{width:8px;height:8px}`; the state is colour only (muted is grey, error red). Real run with mic:"error": pill says "Ready" with a red dot; hovering shows the tooltip "Microphone problem" (x/tip.png). voice.ts keeps the detail only for the settings window. micShown (main.ts:116) excludes starting, downloading and needs-models.
findings.fix: Give each state a shape as well as a colour (slashed mic for muted, "!" for error) and a role="img" aria-label. On error, put "Microphone problem" (or the reason) on the pill's idle line and add a menu item "Microphone problem: open Settings…". Show a dot, or "Voice isn't set up", while models are missing.

findings.title: No text-size control for the overlay, bubble, cards, ask box or command and prompt windows (11-14 px fixed)
findings.scenario: A low-vision user raises the OS text size. Ember's floating surfaces do not follow it: the bubble body is 14 px, steps 13 px, hints and chips 11-12 px, and the ask box key hints about 10.5 px. The overlay, handle and ask box cannot be zoomed (no focus, no menu); the fixed 440x300 prompt and the command windows can be zoomed but scale into clipped content. The 'Size' setting scales only the character.
findings.evidence: Type tokens in ember.css:20-27 and bubble.ts:186, 282, 227 use fixed px. Windows are created fixed-size (windows.ts:76-92). No setting for text size exists in settings.ts.
findings.fix: Add a 'Text size' setting (or follow the OS scale) that multiplies the type tokens and the bubble's CSS, and let the prompt and command windows grow with it.

findings.title: Ember's Calm setting does not reach the Ask, command, prompt and desk windows
findings.scenario: Calm mode is meant to mean 'nothing springs or slides', and html.calm is the only hook that stops the shared controls. Only home, handle and overlay set it (handle/main.ts:34, overlay/main.ts:81, home/main.ts:47). The command, prompt, Ask and desk pages never receive the setting (their preloads expose nothing about settings). With Calm on and the OS preference off, the .btn press spring (transform 220ms var(--spring-snappy)), the hover filter fades and the desk's button transitions still run in those windows. The effect is small, but the setting's promise is not kept.
findings.evidence: grep -rn calm over app/renderer shows toggles only in handle, overlay and home. Animation counts via document.getAnimations() with Calm only: overlay 0, handle 0, home 0, so the three wired windows behave (motion.mjs). The other four windows have no calm hook and rely on prefers-reduced-motion alone; ember.css:187 and :194 give .btn its transform and transition.
findings.fix: Broadcast the settings' reduceMotion to every page (main already sends settings to the overlay and handle) and toggle html.calm there, or have main insert the CSS with webContents.insertCSS for the four pages when the setting is on.
